A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TODSynth/CRFM work. Their complete main texts, references, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-synthesis and downstream segmentation experiments on FUSU-4k and LoveDA, including ablations and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports class-specific segmentation results in Appendix Table 6.

M1.justification: The architecture and overall CRFM procedure are retained. However, v2's Equation 12 and new Algorithm 1 explicitly subtract the loss gradient, while unchanged Appendix Equation 18 uses a positive-gradient correction. The PDFs do not resolve whether the newly explicit subtraction corrects documentation or changes the implemented update.

E1.justification: FUSU-4k and LoveDA coverage is retained. The new analysis concerns Orchard, Public Management and Storage, which already appear among the FUSU classes in v1's Figure 4; no new dataset, population or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their comparator sets. New Table 6 reuses the PSPNet baseline, FreeMask and SD v3.5 already evaluated in Table 1. Its different citation for SD v3.5 does not establish a different comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 6 extends evaluation reporting to individual-class IoU and accuracy for three selected rare categories, complementing the aggregate metrics previously reported. Existing data splits, training budgets, preprocessing and sampling-step settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 examines performance on three rare classes through Table 6. Existing control-strategy ablations, segmentation-model sensitivity tests and sampling/mode-collapse analyses remain; the former B.3 becomes B.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for the results. The existing statement about fixing synthesis seeds is unchanged, and Table 6 adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds class-specific results absent from v1. TODSynth's IoU/accuracy pairs are 41.88/55.37 for Orchard, 42.79/58.00 for Public Management and 40.10/56.91 for Storage; the corresponding SD v3.5 Storage scores are 33.86/49.54. Tables 1–5 and existing qualitative results are unchanged. These are additional results, not performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Equation 12 replaces an ill-formed equality between a gradient operator and cross-entropy with an explicit negative-gradient definition of the rectification vector. This is a localized mathematical correction, without new proofs or assumptions. Equation 18 retains the positive-gradient expression, leaving the sign convention unresolved.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about unified triple attention, early task-guided CRFM sampling and improved segmentation through synthetic data.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.3 interprets rare-class gains as correcting biased or blurry guidance under data scarcity and restoring category boundaries and high-frequency details. Existing limitations concerning segmenter sensitivity, excessive correction, mode collapse and synthetic-data diversity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds explicit CRFM pseudocode covering inputs, latent prediction, VAE decoding, conditional loss, differentiation with respect to velocity and the returned update. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware information and code-access statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 58 referenced works and retain their related-work positioning, including the distinction from FlowEdit and SplitFlow. Changed citation back-references reflect document reflow.

P1.justification: v2 adds an acknowledgement, introduces the pseudocode in Appendix A and inserts the rare-class subsection before the retained sampling analysis. The main narrative and existing appendix prose undergo little rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds the boxed Algorithm 1 and class-comparison Table 6, with accompanying appendix and reference reflow. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–5 retain their existing content and displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the explicit gradient formulation and pseudocode make CRFM easier to follow, while Table 6 supplies targeted evidence for the existing rare-class claim. These are useful, limited gains. Equation 18's unresolved sign convention and interpretations about restored boundaries and fine detail that are not directly tested by the new scores limit the improvement; the original benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
